create.name: Wild Heart Meditation Center
create.bio:
Wild Heart Meditation Center is a non-profit Buddhist community in East Nashville, Tennessee, rooted in early Buddhist teaching and the Western insight tradition. Its story starts in 2010, when founding teacher Dave Smith began a weekly beginners' sit at a local dharma centre that sometimes drew nobody at all; the group grew, became a non-profit in 2013 and opened its present centre on Gallatin Pike in 2017. Rev. Mikey Noechel, ordained as a lay dharma teacher by Ven. Pannavati and Ven. Pannadipa, is now guiding teacher and co-director, and Andrew Chapman, his predecessor in that role, still teaches groups, workshops and study courses.

The name draws on the idea of rewilding: practice as a return of the heart to its natural, unhindered state. Most of what happens is free and drop-in. Silent sits run on weekday mornings, there are evening classes with a guided meditation, a talk and open discussion, and groups for people of colour, LGBTQIA+ practitioners and women. A team of trained facilitators supports the teachers, a sister group meets weekly in Detroit, and longer silent retreats are held at a rented retreat centre. Talks are shared through a podcast and on YouTube.

courses.title: THE UNIFICATION OF MIND Cultivation of Samadhi Silent Meditation Retreat with Mikey Noechel and Andrew Chapman
courses.description: A five-day silent winter retreat with the centre's two senior teachers, devoted to gathering and steadying the mind. As distraction quietens, the teaching turns towards the insight that a collected mind makes possible.

free_resources.title: Weekly Programming
free_resources.description: The centre's weekly timetable of drop-in sessions in Nashville and on Zoom: early-morning silent sits, evening classes with meditation, talk and discussion, and affinity groups. No registration is needed for most.

free_resources.title: WHMC Podcast
free_resources.description: Recorded talks by Wild Heart's teachers and facilitators, offering down-to-earth Buddhist teaching and instruction for ordinary daily life.
